findings.title: Error IDs zipped against nodestore results by position rather than by key
findings.body: `fetch_error_details` pairs `error_ids` with `nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids).values()` by position. `get_multi` returns a dict keyed by node_id, and nothing guarantees it preserves request order. Some backends return results in storage order, and duplicate IDs collapse into one key. When the order differs, error titles and messages get attached to the wrong event IDs. Look each result up with `events.get(node_id)` for its corresponding error_id instead.

findings.title: Error timestamps (seconds) compared against rrweb event timestamps (milliseconds)
findings.body: Nodestore event `timestamp` is epoch seconds, while recording-segment (rrweb) events carry `timestamp` in epoch milliseconds. The merge loop compares the two directly, so every error looks earlier than every breadcrumb. All errors are emitted at the start of the log instead of in chronological order. The tests only pass because the fixtures use second-based breadcrumb timestamps. Normalize both values to the same unit before comparing.

findings.title: Full error list is injected into every paginated page
findings.body: `analyze_recording_segments` receives the complete `error_events` list through `functools.partial` and runs once per page of segments. Each page drains any errors not yet emitted onto the end of its logs. As a result, every page's Seer request contains all of the replay's errors, including ones that belong to other segment ranges. Summaries for later pages are polluted with duplicated, out-of-range errors. Filter errors to the time range of the current page's segments.

findings.title: Migrations turned into no-ops that point to a 0921 migration not included in the PR
findings.body: Both 0917 and 0920 now do nothing and tell readers to see `0921_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_rerevised.py`, but this PR does not add that migration. If it does not land alongside this change, org-visibility saved searches are never converted to GroupSearchView. The comments also reference a file that does not exist. The 0917 migration test was deleted and nothing replaces it.

findings.title: Feature-flagged table widget renders with hardcoded empty data
findings.body: When `use-table-widget-visualization` is enabled, `TableWidgetVisualization` is passed `columns={[]}` and `tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}}`. The real `result.data` and `result.meta` are ignored. Every table widget for orgs with the flag will render blank. Pass the actual query results through, or keep the flag off until that wiring is done.

findings.title: HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES only applied when a search query is entered
findings.body: The memo returns the unfiltered sorted list early when `searchQuery` is empty. The `!HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES.includes(...)` filter therefore only runs during a search. In the default view, `is_segment`, `project_id` and `received` are still shown. Apply the hidden filter before the early return.

findings.title: Per-issue recommended-event lookup when building PR comments
findings.body: `get_environment_info` calls `issue.get_recommended_event()` for every issue in the comment. That is a separate Snuba/nodestore query per issue, done serially inside the comment task. It adds N extra queries per PR comment. Any failure is swallowed silently at info level, so the environment just disappears from the comment without notice.

findings.title: Mutual-exclusion validation of age/timestamp uses truthiness
findings.body: The age/timestamp checks use `self.initial_data.get(...)` as a truthy test, so a value of `0` counts as absent. For example, `age: 0` together with a `timestamp` passes validation. A report with neither `age` nor `timestamp` is also accepted, even though both specs require one of them. Use `'age' in self.initial_data` and add an object-level `validate` that requires exactly one of the two fields.

findings.title: Header alignment computed from display name instead of field key
findings.body: `fieldAlignment(column.name, ...)` uses the column's display name. When custom names are supplied, such as 'Count of Span Duration', alignment detection for aggregate fields fails. The header then aligns differently from the body cells, which are rendered by `column.key`. Use `column.key` instead.
